## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:sweep`'s `## Next Actions` block (`plugin/skills/sweep/SKILL.md`) renders in a
fixed order: the top `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention` pick (when present, replacing the
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` slot per the precedence rule) -> `/claude-tweaks:dispatch {grants}` ->
`/claude-tweaks:tidy --approve` -> `/claude-tweaks:backlog attention`.

`docs/REGISTRY.md` line addition, three stale `bot:in-progress` label removals on issues whose
claims were already stale/released) -- yet `tidy --approve` rendered third in the Next Actions
block, after a `backlog refine #N` re-authorization pick and a `dispatch` call that kicks off
new autonomous builds. The user flagged this live as counter-intuitive: closing out a fully
vetted, zero-judgment batch should be the cheapest, fastest thing to clear -- not buried behind

## Current State

Dispatch (and/or `/build`'s worktree setup) does not appear to check for an existing open PR on a record before claiming and building it fresh, even when that PR's own run-marker shows it already reached `pending-review` under a prior run.

Observed on #1058: a run on 2026-08-28 (`2026-08-28T080617-record-1058`) completed build/test/review and reached `pending-review`, opening draft PR #1602 on branch `worktree-dispatch-record-1058` — then sat unmerged for about a week. A fresh dispatch run on 2026-09-04 (`2026-09-04T080101-record-1058`) claimed and rebuilt #1058 from scratch on a freshly created local branch with the SAME deterministic name, producing a second, fully-diverged commit history for the identical fix. `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` documents a Step 1.6 "Remote-only stale branch check" that is supposed to catch a same-name branch left on origin by a prior attempt and stop for a human decision before `EnterWorktree` ever runs — but the 2026-09-04 run's build phase evidently never hit that stop (or it was bypassed), since it proceeded to materialize, build, and commit without incident.

Root cause not yet diagnosed — candidates: (a) the claim on #1058 was released once the 2026-08-28 run reached `pending-review` (per the documented "reconciler finishes armed/pending-review later" model), making the record eligible for dispatch selection again despite an open PR already existing for it; (b) `build/worktree-setup.md`'s Step 1.5/1.6 stale-branch checks have a gap that let a remote-only collision through; (c) dispatch's own selection query doesn't exclude records with an already-open PR.

## Deliverables

- Diagnose why the 2026-09-04 run's build phase did not stop at `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 1.6 (or equivalent) despite PR #1602 already existing on the same deterministic branch name.
- Either: (a) have dispatch's selection query skip records with an existing open PR (reuse it instead of reclaiming), or (b) fix the Step 1.6 stale-branch check gap that let this run past it, or both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record with an existing open PR from a prior run cannot be silently re-claimed and rebuilt from scratch on a colliding branch name; either the existing PR is reused/resumed, or a human is stopped for a decision before any new work is committed.

Origin: discovered during #1058's own `/flow review,polish,wrap-up` run (2026-09-04T080101-record-1058), which found PR #1602 already open and pending-review for the same issue

- `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` — 40853 B

- `plugin/skills/journey-health/SKILL.md` — 40798 B
- `plugin/skills/specify/SKILL.md` — 40948 B

Pick whichever fits this project's actual maintenance cadence better; both are legitimate fixes for the same underlying gap.
- [ ] If (a) is chosen for any file, verify the corresponding prose-conformance tests (pinned section/line assertions elsewhere in the suite) still pass — several of these files are conformance-tested outside `context-cost.test.js` itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. None of the five named files sits above 90% of `CEILING_BYTES` (`plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js`) on `main`.

Surface: backend

## Overview

The allocation half of port isolation. A registry module leases one block of 10 consecutive ports per checkout from a fixed pool (20000-29999, 1000 blocks), keyed by the checkout's real path (`fs.realpathSync`), verified free by binding every port in the block; an env-file module writes the block as a managed region; a CLI exposes allocate/status/release/env. Pure Node, cross-platform — no `lsof`, no shell. This unit ships no consumer: nothing calls it until Unit 2.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 7

## Non-Goals

- The `port-services` policy key (Unit 2 — this unit takes `--services` on the CLI only)
- SessionStart integration, statusline, release-on-reap (Units 2-3)
- `/init` rewrite (Unit 4)
- Any dev-url-detection change (Unit 5)
- A configurable pool range
- Relocating ports outside the pool

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/file-lock.js` exports `acquireLock/releaseLock/withLock` (mkdir mutex, 500 ms wait, 5 s stale reclaim) — reuse, never add a lock.
- `plugin/bin/lib/json-store.js` exports `readJsonFile(path,{fallback})` (degrade-open) and `writeJsonFile(path,data)` (mkdir parent + `atomic-write.js` tmp-and-rename) — reuse for the registry.
- `plugin/bin/lib/{name}/` is the flat multi-file module convention (CLAUDE.md Structure); `plugin/bin/*.js` CLIs follow the `run(argv, deps)` seam, exit-code vocabulary and injectable runner in the repo's `gh-api-module-pattern` skill (`.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/` — read its CLI wrapper contract section; `plugin/bin/stage-item.js` + `plugin/bin/lib/stage-item/` is the closest sibling to copy).
- `~/.claude-tweaks/` already exists as claude-tweaks' home-dir location (`/init` Step 8 installs `~/.claude-tweaks/bin/statusline.js`).
- Tests: `tests/bin-lib/atomic-write.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/stage-item/` show the `node --test` style (tmp dirs via `fs.mkdtempSync`, injectable deps, no mocking library). `npm test` picks up `tests/bin-lib/{x}/` recursively.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` — `registryPath({home = os.homedir()})` → `{home}/.claude-tweaks/ports.json`; `readRegistry`, `allocate(checkoutPath, {services, home, probe})`, `release(checkoutPath, {home})`, `status({home})`, `gc(registry)`; constants `POOL_BASE = 20000`, `POOL_END = 29999`, `BLOCK_SIZE = 10`; every read-modify-write inside `withLock(registryPath + '.lock')`.
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/ports/probe.js` — `isFree(port, {host = '127.0.0.1'})` via `net.createServer().listen(port, host)` then close (resolves `true` on listen, `false` on `EADDRINUSE`/`EACCES`); `blockFree(base, {size})` = all ports free.
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/ports/env-file.js` — `serviceVars(services, base)` → ordered `[[name, value]]` with the first service → `PORT`, later → `{UPPER_SNAKE}_PORT` (sanitize the service name by replacing every non-alphanumeric run with `_`, then uppercasing — e.g. `my-db` → `MY_DB_PORT`), offsets 0..n-1; `mergeManagedRegion(existingText, lines)` replaces the region between `# claude-tweaks:ports begin` and `# claude-tweaks:ports end` (marker lines exact, first line reads `# claude-tweaks:ports begin — managed; edit port-services in .claude-tweaks/policy.yml instead`), appends the region when absent, preserves every other line byte-for-byte including CRLF; `writeEnvFiles(checkoutPath, vars)` writes `.env.local`, and also `.env` when `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, or `compose.yaml` exists in the checkout root.
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/ports/cli.js` + `plugin/bin/ports.js` — subcommands `allocate [--path P] [--services a,b,c]`, `status [--path P]`, `release [--path P]`, `env [--path P]`; `--path` defaults to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of cwd via the injectable runner; `env` prints `KEY=value` lines only; exit 0 success, 2 malformed invocation, 3 pool exhausted, 4 registry unwritable.
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/ports/{registry,probe,env-file,cli}.test.js` covering every AC below.
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md` — one `plugin/bin/lib/ports/` row in the lib table and one `node plugin/bin/ports.js ...` line in the CLI list, same shape as the `log-decision.js` entries.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Fresh registry → `allocate` returns base 20000 and writes `{version:1, leases:{"20000":{path, project, services, leased}}}` where `path` is the realpath, `services` is the requested service-name array (so `status`/`env` can reconstruct `KEY=value` lines without a repeated `--services` flag), and `leased` is ISO-8601 UTC.
2. With a test listener bound on 20003, `allocate` from a fresh registry skips block 20000 and returns 20010.
3. Two `allocate` calls for the same path return the same block and leave one lease (idempotent).
4. A lease whose `path` no longer exists on disk is dropped by the next `allocate`/`status` (gc), and its block becomes allocatable.
5. Two concurrent allocators (child processes, distinct paths, same `home`) receive distinct blocks — no duplicate base in the registry afterwards.
6. `release(path)` removes the lease from the registry only (it does not touch `.env`/`.env.local` — those are Unit 3's reap-time job; a manually-released checkout keeps stale values in its env file until the next `allocate`/`ensure` overwrites them); `release` on an unknown path exits 0 and reports nothing.
7. A corrupt `ports.json` (invalid JSON) is renamed to a filesystem-safe filename embedding the timestamp — `ports.json.corrupt-{ISO timestamp with every ':' replaced by '-'}` (ISO-8601 colons are illegal in Windows filenames, and AC13 requires this to pass on Windows) — and a fresh registry is written; the rename is reported on stderr.
8. Pool exhausted (test by injecting a probe that reports every block bound) → error `PORTS_EXHAUSTED`, exit 3, registry unchanged.
9. `serviceVars(['web','api','db'], 20010)` → `[['PORT','20010'],['API_PORT','20011'],['DB_PORT','20012']]`.
10. `mergeManagedRegion` on a file with foreign lines above and below the region replaces only the region; running it twice yields identical bytes; a CRLF input stays CRLF; an input without the region gets it appended after a trailing newline.
11. `.env` is written only when a Compose file exists in the checkout root; `.env.local` always.
12. The CLI's `env` output for a leased path is exactly the managed lines without markers; for a path with no lease, `env` prints nothing and exits 0 (there is nothing to report, not an error); unknown subcommand or unparseable `--services` exits 2 with a usage line on stderr.
13. All of the above pass on Windows (the author's machine) and POSIX — no `lsof`, no shell pipes in the module.

## Technical Approach

Registry shape `{ "version": 1, "leases": { "<base>": { "path": "<realpath>", "project": "<basename of main checkout>", "services": ["<name>", ...], "leased": "<ISO>" } } }`. `allocate`: `withLock` → `readJsonFile(fallback=null)`; if null and the file exists, do the corrupt-rename; `gc` → if lease for path exists return it → walk bases `POOL_BASE + k*BLOCK_SIZE` skipping leased bases, `await blockFree(base)`; first free → write lease → `writeJsonFile` → return `{base, ports:[base..base+9], vars}` → then write env files. The bind-probe is async (net) while `withLock` is sync; run the probe loop inside the lock using a sync-compatible approach: either make `withLock` usage an explicit `acquireLock`/`try{await}/finally{releaseLock}` pair, or probe candidate blocks before acquiring the lock and re-verify the chosen block's registry status after acquiring it — pick the acquire/await/release pair and document it in the module header. Whichever pair is chosen, when the *post-lock* re-verification finds the candidate block now taken (a concurrent allocator won the race), loop to the next candidate block rather than aborting — the loop only ends at pool exhaustion (AC8). `acquireLock`/`withLock` failing to acquire the lock at all (timeout) must never let `allocate` fall through and write unlocked — `file-lock.js`'s own default is fail-open (the caller proceeds unlocked on a missed lock), but that default would let two racing allocators both write, violating AC5's "no duplicate base" guarantee; `allocate` overrides it for its own read-modify-write by retrying the acquire up to the lock's existing 500 ms/5 s bounds and, if still unacquired, failing with a distinct `PORTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT` error (mapped to CLI exit 4, "registry unwritable") rather than proceeding. `project` = `path.basename(mainCheckoutRoot)`, resolved via `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-detect.js`'s `mainCheckoutRoot(cwd)` when the path is a linked worktree, else the path's own basename.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/ports.js` — new CLI entry
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` — new
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/probe.js` — new
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/env-file.js` — new
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/cli.js` — new
- `plugin/bin/lib/file-lock.js` — consumed, unchanged
- `plugin/bin/lib/json-store.js` — consumed, unchanged
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-detect.js` — consumed for `mainCheckoutRoot`
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/registry.test.js` — new
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/probe.test.js` — new
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/env-file.test.js` — new
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/cli.test.js` — new
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — two rows

### Package Dependencies

- none — Node built-ins (`net`, `fs`, `os`, `path`) only.

## Gotchas

- Key the registry on `os.homedir()`, never on `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`~/.claude-accounts/<slug>` — ports are a machine resource shared across accounts.
- Realpath the checkout before keying (Windows drive-letter case and symlinked worktrees).
- Bind on `127.0.0.1`; on Windows a port bound on `0.0.0.0` by another process still fails the loopback bind, which is the desired signal.
- The lock helper is synchronous and the probe is async — see Technical Approach; never hold the lock across an unbounded await without the 500 ms/5 s bounds already in `file-lock.js`.
- Don't write `.env`/`.env.local` when the lease was found but env content is unchanged (avoid mtime churn that Vite watches).
- Never `console.log` from the module — only the CLI prints.
- When the env file is not writable, the lease is still recorded in the registry and the write failure is reported on stderr (never a hard error — `allocate`'s own exit code stays 0 when called from the CLI's `allocate` subcommand) — a caller reading via `ports.js env` still gets the correct values, since `env` reads the registry directly (including the persisted `services` array) rather than the file it failed to write.
- `status({home})` is not purely read-only: it runs the same dead-path gc as `allocate` (AC4) and persists the pruned registry as a side effect. Treat that persist as best-effort — a write failure during `status`'s own gc is reported (stderr) but never thrown; `status` still returns the in-memory (already-pruned) view to its caller.
- CLI exit 4 ("registry unwritable") covers both a registry write that fails after the lock is held (permissions, disk full) and a `PORTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (the lock itself could not be acquired within its existing 500 ms/5 s bounds) — see Technical Approach.

## Decision Rationale

An env override alone answers only *how* an app receives a port, not *who chooses the value* — allocation is what avoids collisions, and three strategies were weighed:

| Strategy | Verdict |
|----------|---------|
| Deterministic hash of the checkout path → port block | No coordination needed, but hash collisions among a few dozen projects in a few thousand slots are likely, and it is blind to foreign processes already bound on the derived ports. Rejected on its own. |
| **Machine-wide lease registry with bind-probe verification** | One file per machine; allocation takes the lowest block that is unleased *and* verified free by binding every port. Keyed by checkout path, so worktrees of one repo and unrelated repos draw from the same pool. **Chosen.** |
| OS-assigned port 0 plus discovery file | Collision-free by construction, but most frameworks and Compose handle it badly and it is the most invasive project change of the three — every consuming project would need a discovery step, not just an env read. Rejected. |

**Blocks, not single ports.** The unit is a 10-port block per checkout rather than one port per service, because Vite's (and Next's) silent auto-bump-on-collision behavior is what causes the worst failure mode named in the design: a frontend bumps from 3000 to 3001, but its proxy target is still a fixed backend port that belongs to a *different* worktree — silent cross-wiring, not a crash. Leasing a block per checkout and deriving every sibling service's port as a fixed offset from that block's base keeps a checkout's own frontend and backend wired to each other even when the checkout's block itself had to move (see Unit 2's reallocation behavior). A single-port-at-a-time scheme cannot make that guarantee, since nothing ties a second service's allocation to the first's.

# Ledger item 2 — staged backlog proposal

**Category:** bug

Origin: /claude-tweaks:wrap-up run for record #1222 (Phase 2 curation, Journeys row), 2026-09-02.
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger — pre-existing, unrelated to #1222's own diff, and a proper fix needs a new regression test in a file with no existing coverage of this function.

## Current State

`parseJourneyFilesList` in `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` (used by the `plan` CLI command's
`buildJourneyFrontmatter`, which feeds `engine-plan.js`'s `resolveFrontmatterOverlapScope` for the
Journeys curation row) splits journey frontmatter on `\n` only. A journey file with CRLF (`\r\n`)
line endings — `docs/journeys/verify-wrap-ups-closure-checklist-900.md` is a live example in this
repo — leaves each `- path` line in the parsed frontmatter array carrying a trailing `\r`. The
match regex `/^\s*-\s+(.+)$/` cannot consume it: JavaScript regex `.` excludes `\r` as a line
terminator, and `$` (without the `m` flag) requires the true end of the string, not "before a
trailing `\r`". The regex match fails entirely on the first `- path` line, the loop's `if (!m)
break;` fires immediately, and the whole `files:` list silently parses to `[]`.

Net effect: any CRLF-encoded journey drops out of `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` Phase 2's Journeys-row
candidate scan (`journey-curation.md`'s J1 check) — the wrap-up run proceeds as if that journey has
zero overlap with the current diff, even when its own `files:` frontmatter names files the diff
actually touched. Reproduced live: isolating `parseJourneyFilesList` + `gatherFacts` against
`docs/journeys/verify-wrap-ups-closure-checklist-900.md` (frontmatter lists
`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` and `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js`, both changed by
record #1222) returns `parsed files: []` and `overlap: false`, even though
`changed.has('plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js')` is `true`.

No functional harm was caused in this specific run — the journey text was independently confirmed
accurate by direct read during the same wrap-up pass — but the candidate computation itself is
silently wrong on any CRLF checkout, which is common on Windows without a normalizing
`.gitattributes` entry for `docs/journeys/*.md`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Make `parseJourneyFilesList` (`plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js`) CRLF-tolerant — e.g. normalize
      the content (`content.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')`, or split on `/\r\n|\n/`) before the existing
      line-based parse, rather than reworking the match regex line by line.
- [ ] Add a regression test pinning CRLF frontmatter parsing for this function (no existing test
      file covers it today — check `tests/wrap-up-engine-run-dir-anchoring.test.js` and
      `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/` for the right home, or add a new focused test file).
- [ ] Consider whether other frontmatter/markdown parsers in `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/` and
      `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` share the same LF-only assumption (e.g. the Skills/Docs rows'
      own file-reading paths) — scope this only if a quick grep turns up an obviously shared helper;
      otherwise file a separate record rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A journey file with CRLF line endings and a `files:` frontmatter list correctly contributes its
   listed files to the Journeys row's candidate-overlap computation (verified by the new
   regression test).
2. Existing LF-encoded journeys continue to parse identically (no regression).
3. `npm test` stays fully green.

---

Origin: review
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

The materiality digest mechanism (`_shared/materiality-floor.md`, shipped by #1261) has three gaps only surfaced once real adopters (#1262) started routing findings to it — none fixable within #1262's own scope since #1262's Non-Goals bar changing the contract itself, and two require actual code (not prose).

## Current State

#1262's final whole-branch review (spec #1262, "Migrate the ten adopter files to cite `_shared/materiality-floor.md`") found:

1. **No `Defer-reason:` vocabulary for the four health sweeps' digest entries.** `_shared/materiality-floor.md`'s Entry format makes `Defer-reason: {value}` a mandatory field, and that value's vocabulary is defined by `_shared/deferral-gate.md` — but `code-health`, `docs-health`, `harness-health`, and `journey-health` never run through the deferral gate at all (they file spec-shaped issues directly via `recordPayload`/`specShapedBody`, per #1262's own Current State: "These do NOT cite the deferral gate"). There is no defined value these four sweeps can legitimately write into a materiality-digest entry's `Defer-reason:` field. #1262's own citations correctly route below-floor health-sweep findings to the digest, but leave this field unaddressed — an agent executing the sweep has no well-formed value to write.

2. **No dedup on materiality digest entries — spurious promotion after repeated firings.** The pre-existing per-origin cap digest (`_shared/health-filing-digest.md`) solves this explicitly via a fingerprint fold (`expandDigestFingerprints`) that lets a re-encountered finding dedupe against its own existing digest entry instead of re-appending. The materiality digest has no equivalent — `tidy/digest-sweep.md` has no dedup step of its own. A below-floor finding that a scheduled health sweep re-encounters on every firing gets a fresh entry appended each time; `digest-sweep.md`'s own cluster-promotion procedure fires once ≥3 entries share the same `{area}` — so a genuinely low-value, repeatedly-recurring finding becomes a first-class issue after 3 firings, inverting the contract's entire purpose (reducing issue volume for low-materiality findings).

3. **The digest comment URL and `filed/digested/cap` accounting never reach any adopter's own summary.** `_shared/materiality-floor.md`'s Deliverables state "the run's single digest comment URL... appears once in the caller's own summary output," but none of the ten adopter files' report/handoff/summary formats were updated to actually surface it, and the four health sweeps' existing `filed: N, digested: M, cap: {CAP}` throttle line (from the pre-existing cap-digest mechanism) does not count materiality-digest routings at all — so a run's actual digest activity is invisible in every caller's own output.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide and document a `Defer-reason:` (or equivalent) vocabulary answer for direct-filing producers (the four health sweeps today; possibly other future non-gate-routed adopters) — either extend `bin/lib/issues/record.js`'s closed `DEFER_REASONS` set with a value describing "no deferral gate applies, filed directly by a proactive sweep," or define an explicit, contract-stated exception in `_shared/materiality-floor.md` for this producer class.
- [ ] Design and implement a dedup mechanism for materiality digest entries — likely a fingerprint-based fold analogous to `_shared/health-filing-digest.md`'s `expandDigestFingerprints`, reconciled with `tidy/digest-sweep.md`'s existing cluster-promotion threshold so a genuinely-recurring-but-still-low-value finding does not spuriously promote.
- [ ] Wire the digest comment URL and a digest-specific count into each adopter's own summary/report format — likely ten distinct small edits (one per adopter's own summary shape) plus updating the four health sweeps' `filed/digested/cap` line to also report materiality-digest routings separately from cap-digest routings.
- [ ] `tests/materiality-floor-conformance.test.js` and/or a new suite covering the dedup mechanism and vocabulary answer once designed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A health-sweep-originated materiality digest entry has a well-formed `Defer-reason:` (or documented equivalent) value, with a test pinning it.
2. Re-running a sweep against an already-digested, unchanged finding does not append a second entry, and does not contribute toward cluster-promotion's ≥3 threshold a second time.
3. At least one adopter's own summary output surfaces the run's digest comment URL when a digest routing occurred this run; the four health sweeps' throttle line reports a materiality-digest count distinct from the cap-digest count.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Filed by #1262's own final whole-branch review — that spec's scope was citation-only (per its Non-Goals, "No change to the contract itself"); these three gaps require either a contract amendment or new code, both out of scope there. Item 2 (dedup) is closely related to #1273's existing scope (tidy's digest-sweep wiring/mechanics) — coordinate with or fold into that issue if picked up around the same time, since both touch `tidy/digest-sweep.md`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/materiality-floor.md` — Entry format, Defer-reason field, Deliverables' summary-surfacing requirement
- `bin/lib/issues/record.js` — `DEFER_REASONS` closed vocabulary (if extended)
- `plugin/skills/tidy/digest-sweep.md` — cluster-promotion mechanism, needs dedup
- `plugin/skills/code-health/filing.md`, `docs-health/SKILL.md`, `harness-health/filing.md`, `journey-health/SKILL.md` — Defer-reason gap + summary-surfacing
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md`, `wrap-up/residue-sweep.md`, `wrap-up/leftover-routing.md`, `reflect/full-mode.md`, `reflect/hindsight-mode.md`, `visual-review/browser-review.md` — summary-surfacing (these already have a Defer-reason via the deferral gate, so item 1 doesn't apply to them)

Surface: backend

## Current State

#1674 bounded `hasMaterializeCommit`'s git log to `{integration}..HEAD` so a materialize commit inherited from an unrelated merged run stops arming the IL-131 gate. `resolveIntegrationBranch` (`worktree-reap.js`) resolves that name from two sources only: an `integration-branch:` policy key, or `origin/HEAD`.

Neither is available in a no-remote `local-merge` project: there is no `origin`, and the policy key is normally unset (`policy-schema.js` documents it as needed only when the active branch is not the default). Such a repo still has a real local integration branch that materialize commits merge into — it is simply not *resolvable*. #1674 falls back to the pre-fix unbounded walk there, so the false positive it exists to fix persists for that whole project class.

This was reproduced during review: a bare no-remote repo, a materialize-shaped commit on `main`, then `git worktree add` a fresh branch off that HEAD. `resolveIntegrationBranch(wt)` returns `null`; `hasMaterializeCommit(wt, runDir)` returns `true` — the fresh worktree is armed against a commit it never made.

A second, related gap: `resolveIntegrationBranch` returns a **local** branch name, which can lag `origin/{integration}`. When HEAD has already merged `origin/{integration}` in — which `_shared/worktree-setup.md`'s post-creation catch-up does routinely — the lagging local ref leaves those merged-in commits inside the range and reproduces the same inherited-history arm. `review/code-mode-steps.md` states this repo's own house rule: never trust a bare local branch name, because a long-lived worktree's local tracking branch routinely drifts behind its remote.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A third resolution source for the range bound when policy and `origin/HEAD` both come up empty — e.g. a local default-branch probe (`main`/`master`, or the branch the worktree was created from), used only for this bound.
- [ ] A decision on the stale-local-ref case: either resolve `origin/{integration}` when the remote-tracking ref already exists locally (no fetch needed), or document why the local name is accepted.
- [ ] Tests covering a no-remote repo with inherited history (currently returns `true`, should return `false`) and a local ref lagging its remote-tracking counterpart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a no-remote repo, a fresh worktree with zero commits of its own is NOT armed by a materialize commit it inherited.
2. A worktree carrying its own unmerged materialize commit is still armed (the #991 protection, unchanged).
3. No new failure mode disarms the gate: any resolution failure still falls back to the unbounded walk rather than returning `false` (#1674's own correction).
4. `npm test` passes, including the existing `hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate` suite unmodified.

## Gotchas

Adding a resolution source is new behavior in a helper shared with `run-integrity.js`, not a range bound on an existing call — #1674's whole stated scope.

## Original request

Origin: `/claude-tweaks:review #1674`, Step 3 — both agents of the lens-3c reproduction pair, one with a direct reproduction that refuted the reviewing agent's own initial justification ("the false positive cannot arise where no integration branch exists" — wrong; a no-remote repo has a real local integration branch, it is merely unresolvable). #1674 shipped the correct conservative behavior (fall back, keep the gate armed) and corrected its own overclaiming comment and docs rather than papering over the gap. Filed via the `/claude-tweaks:flow #1463,#1672,#1673,#1674` consolidated Review Console.

Its own docstring (lines 4-6, 35-37) claims this check is 'reused verbatim from _shared/work-record.md's Spec-shaped body section' and 'the one check that composer does not make' by hand elsewhere, but it is not verbatim: work-record.md line 258 and specify/shaping-mode.md line 88 both state the preserved '## Original request' section (shaping-mode's byte-exact copy of the record's original title/body) is explicitly EXEMPT from the placeholder check, citing issue #1240 by name ('the preserved copy is exempt from the spec-shaped-body placeholder check (#1240), so preservation stays byte-exact even when the original text carries a literal TBD/TODO/ambiguity marker'). The sibling implementation bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js already carries this exact fix: it defines ORIGINAL_REQUEST_RE, slices the body at that heading, and only tests the 'authored' (pre-heading) text against PLACEHOLDER_RE before flagging 'unresolved-placeholder' (materialize-format.js lines 12-18, 46-48). compose.js has no equivalent slice — it is the one caller of this canonical check that never received the #1240 fix. This is live: specify/record-creation.md line 204 invokes `bin/compose-record.js ... --require-shaped` for shaping-mode's sub-issue creation, the exact flow that appends '## Original request' per shaping-mode.md lines 78-88. If a user's originally captured idea (via /capture, explicitly meant for 'half-formed features' and 'brain dumps') contains a literal 'TBD', 'TODO', or '<!-- ambiguity:' anywhere in its title/body, /specify's shaping mode will preserve it verbatim in '## Original request' and compose-record.js will wrongly exit 4 ('body is not spec-shaped') even though the actually-authored shaped sections have no placeholders — blocking legitimate, compliant sub-issue creation in the automated pipeline.

## Deliverables

In compose.js's validateShaped, mirror materialize-format.js's fix: before scanning for PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS, locate the '## Original request' heading (line-anchored, matching splitSections' own heading regex) and only scan the text before it — the same 'authored' vs. verbatim-preserved split materialize-format.js already implements. Keep the REQUIRED_SECTIONS presence/emptiness checks unchanged (they only ever look at the three named sections, which always precede '## Original request', so they are unaffected). Add a test mirroring the CLI-level scenario: a body with a compliant three-section shape followed by a '## Original request' section containing a literal TBD/TODO/ambiguity marker should validate as ok:true.

## Acceptance Criteria

validateShaped(body) returns {ok:true, gaps:[]} for a body whose three required sections are complete and placeholder-free, but whose '## Original request' section (or any content at/after that heading) contains a literal TBD, TODO, or <!-- ambiguity: marker. A marker in the same position for a body with no '## Original request' heading (or before it) still correctly fails as today. A new test in tests/bin-lib/compose-record/compose.test.js covers this case explicitly. `npm test` passes.

`skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Overview states: "When invoked by `/claude-tweaks:flow`, review runs in **full** mode by default (code + visual)." While performing #1313's final whole-branch review (fix compute-then-exit truncation risk in `plugin/bin/release.js` and `plugin/bin/review-coordination.js` — itself a follow-up to #1176's earlier sweep), the reviewer found that #1313's own sweep enumeration was incomplete. `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js:76` carries the identical idiom:

```js
process.exit(run(process.argv.slice(2)));
```

`run()`'s `build`/`mint` branches end with `deps.stdout(JSON.stringify(result) + '\n'); return 0;` — the same shape #1176/#1313 already fixed elsewhere: a stdout write immediately before returning an integer that then feeds `process.exit()`, which can truncate the write for a piped consumer.

The enumeration was verified exact by the #1313 final reviewer: `process.exit(` appears in exactly three `plugin/bin/*.js` files — `build-review-context.js:76` (this idiom, unfixed), `hooks.js:779` (correctly excluded — uses synchronous `fs.writeSync(1, ...)` with no async flush to lose), and `wrap-up-engine.js:361` (a comment, not a call, not in scope). A GitHub search (`gh issue list --search "build-review-context process.exit"` and `--search "truncation exit in:title"`, both `--state all`) found no existing record for this file.

This matters more than the other two instances: `build-review-context.js` is what `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3 shells out to for its context bundle, and skill prose parses its stdout JSON line.

- In `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js`, change `process.exit(run(process.argv.slice(2)));` to `process.exitCode = run(process.argv.slice(2));`. The call sits inside an existing `try` block whose `catch` already sets `process.exitCode = 1` — that fallback is unaffected, since `process.exit()` never threw there anyway.
- Read `main()`/`run()` in full first, per #1176's own safety rule, to confirm no code after the changed line assumes an immediate hard-stop (the same check #1313 performed for its two files).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The file exits with the same status code as before for a representative success and failure case.
2. `npm test` passes in full.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/hooks.js record-worktree` (bin/hooks.js:150-181) has two compounding gaps discovered live during #923's review+polish+wrap-up dispatch call:

1. **No `--run` validation/requirement.** When `--run` is omitted, `resolveRunArg` falls through to `resolveRunDir`'s "newest non-terminal run" default — which, in a repo with many concurrent pipeline runs (the normal state under this project's own dispatch/flow usage), can resolve to a run directory that has nothing to do with the caller's intent. There is no confirmation, no dry-run, no "which run did you mean" surfaced to the caller.
2. **No flag/usage validation.** `record-worktree --help` (a natural first probe when unsure of a CLI's exact flags) is not recognized as a help request at all — `--help` is silently consumed as `rest[0]`, i.e. the **worktree positional argument**, and the command proceeds to write `{worktree: "<cwd>/--help", status: "active", sessionId: "<current session>"}` into whatever run directory the default resolution above landed on.

Combined, an agent that runs `record-worktree --help` (or any malformed invocation) without an explicit `--run` silently corrupts an unrelated, unowned run's `run-state.json` — overwriting its `worktree` and `sessionId` fields with garbage — with a success message (`claude-tweaks: worktree recorded for {basename}`) that gives no indication anything went wrong. In this incident it clobbered the dispatching session's own standalone bookkeeping run dir (`{ts}-dispatch-standalone`), mid-run, requiring a manual repair (`fs.writeFileSync` to strip the bad fields back out — not git-recoverable, since `run-state.json` is gitignored).

Confirmed still live against the current checkout (`plugin/bin/hooks.js`'s `record-worktree` branch, ~line 243): `resolveRunArg` (line 96) only special-cases the literal `--run` flag — any other `--`-prefixed token in `rest` (e.g. `--help`) still falls straight through to `const worktreeArg = rest[0]` and, when a fallback `runDir` resolves, into the `writeRunState` write path unchanged. `#38`'s earlier fix added `--run <path>` support (explicit-path validation, anchoring under the main checkout, the worktree-local-fallback disclosure) but did not touch this separate flag-as-positional gap.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `record-worktree` (and, for consistency, `record-pr`/`close-run` — same `resolveRunArg` seam) rejects any argv token starting with `--` where a positional path/worktree argument is expected, with a clear usage error, rather than silently accepting it as the value
- [ ] `record-worktree`/`record-pr` require an explicit `--run` (or otherwise refuse to fall back to the "newest non-terminal run" default) — or, if the default must stay for some existing caller, print a loud disclosure line naming which run dir the default resolved to, so a mismatch is at least visible in the tool's own stdout
- [ ] Add `--help`/`-h` handling (or a documented "no such thing as help in this dispatcher" convention consistently applied) so an unrecognized flag can never silently become a positional value

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `record-worktree --help` (no `--run`) exits with a usage error and writes nothing, rather than mutating any run's `run-state.json`
2. `record-worktree <positional-only, no --run>` either refuses (preferred) or prints the resolved run dir's path loudly enough that `node --test`-level fixtures can assert on it
3. A new `tests/bin-lib/hooks/` (or wherever `record-worktree`'s existing suite lives) regression test pins case 1 above
4. `npm test` green — full suite

## Technical Approach

The fix lives in `bin/hooks.js`'s `record-worktree`/`record-pr` branches (bin/hooks.js:150-181, :246-273) and/or the shared `resolveRunArg` helper they both call. Validate `rest[0]` doesn't start with `-` before treating it as a path; consider requiring `--run` outright for both verbs, since every real caller in the skill prose already passes it explicitly (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s citing sites) — the fallback exists for convenience but its failure mode is silent cross-run corruption, which is worse than a hard requirement.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `record-worktree`, `record-pr` command branches
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `resolveRunArg`, `writeRunState`
- Existing test suite for `record-worktree`/`record-pr` (grep for it under `tests/`)

## Gotchas

- `run-state.json` is gitignored, so a corruption from this bug is not git-recoverable — manual repair (as done live in #923's dispatch) is the only remedy today. This raises the value of preventing the corruption over merely detecting it after the fact.
- Any fix must not break the legitimate no-`--run` callers already documented elsewhere in the skill prose (if any exist) — audit call sites before tightening validation.
- `resolveRunArg` (plugin/bin/hooks.js:96) is shared by more callers than just `record-worktree`/`record-pr` — `spec-status`, `close-run`, and others also call it (see the additional `resolveRunArg` call sites in `bin/hooks.js`). A fix placed inside `resolveRunArg` itself changes behavior for all of them; a fix placed only in the `record-worktree`/`record-pr` branches leaves the others as-is. Decide and state which, since the Deliverables only name `record-worktree`/`record-pr`/`close-run` explicitly.

## Decision Rationale

Filed immediately per this project's no-implicit-deferrals rule (`CLAUDE.md`'s Philosophy section) — discovered live during #923's own dispatch execution, real and reproducible, but out of scope for #923's own diff (a `/tmp` session-scoping sweep across `skills/**` prose, unrelated to `bin/hooks.js`'s argument-parsing robustness). Origin: reflect full mode from #1228
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` checks the last assistant text of a SubagentStop-triggering
event against `STATUS_RE` (`^(DONE|DONE_WITH_CONCERNS|NEEDS_CONTEXT|BLOCKED)\b`) and logs a
`contract-violation` event when it doesn't match. When the session receiving this check is itself
running as a background job (dispatched via the Agent tool by an outer orchestrator — e.g. a
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` two-call handoff), every one of that session's own turn boundaries while
waiting on its own parallel Task-tool dispatches is independently checked, even though the
subagent-output-contract's status-line requirement applies only to a dispatched subagent's own
*final* reply — never to the orchestrating session's legitimate interim narration turns. During
record #1228's own review+polish+wrap-up dispatch, 8 lens-review agents plus a code-simplifier
agent were dispatched in parallel; the orchestrating session narrated one line per completion
notification per its own "Narrate" convention. `friction-events.js --run <that run>` returned 15
`contract-violation` events for the run — all 15 are verbatim excerpts of the orchestrating
session's own narration text, not any dispatched agent's reply. All 9 real dispatched Task agents
that run correctly emitted a valid status line as their first reply line; zero genuine violations
occurred. The file's own header comment already documents one known false-positive source ("a
dispatch whose own template specifies a different first-line contract") but not this second class.

## Deliverables

- Extend `subagent-stop.js`'s existing "Known false-positive source" header comment to name this
  second class: a background-job session's own interim narration turns, checked independently of
  its dispatched subagents' replies. Documenting the limitation is sufficient given the hook is
  warn-tier/best-effort and never blocks — no behavioral change required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The false-positive comment block names both known sources.
- A future reader of `events.jsonl`'s `contract-violation` entries for a background-job-orchestrated
  run understands why a high count there does not necessarily indicate genuine subagent contract
  violations.

Surface: backend

## Current State

Dispatch's queue-pull (`SKILL.md` Step 2, driven by `queue-pull-script.md`) selects eligible candidates by label/dependency filters only: **open + `auto:build` + no `bot:*` + no open `Blocked by #N` dependency + unclaimed**. It never checks whether a candidate already has an open, unmerged PR referencing it.

#257 has an open draft PR #869 (build/test/review/wrap-up complete, awaiting a human merge verdict) yet was re-selected by dispatch hours after a prior firing (`2026-08-21T105702-spec-252-257-899-266-316-644-652`) explicitly released its claim on #257 for this exact reason and posted a comment documenting it. This same record's own dispatch reproduced the bug again (run `2026-08-21T181739-record-257`) — a repeatable failure mode, not a one-off.

## Deliverables

- Step 2's eligibility filter additionally excludes any candidate that already has an open PR referencing it via a closing keyword (`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves #N`) or GitHub's native "Development" linkage.
- The exclusion is surfaced in this firing's own reporting, following the existing Blocked-exclusion report's rendering convention (`SKILL.md` Step 3) — a named line when non-empty, silent when nothing was excluded.
- All four selection forms (bare, `next`, `#N`, `#N,#M,...`) inherit the exclusion uniformly, since they all read Step 2's `dispatch-groups.json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record carrying an open PR (draft or ready-for-review) that will close it is excluded from Step 2's eligible pool, even when it still carries `auto:build` and no `bot:*` label.
- The exclusion is reported the same firing it fires, naming the excluded record and the linked PR number.
- Direct `#N` dispatch and the explicit `#N,#M,...` list form both re-check this exclusion against Step 2's live queue — consistent with how they already re-verify `auto:build`/`bot:*` there — rather than only the bare/`next` forms picking it up.
- A record with no linked PR is unaffected — no new false exclusions on the steady-state queue.

## Technical Approach

Add a linked-PR check to `queue-pull-script.md`'s eligibility pipeline, parallel to the existing `partitionByOpenBodyBlockers`/`partitionByOpenNativeBlockers` pair in `record.js`. Fetch, per eligible candidate, whether it has an open PR that will close it via the GraphQL `Issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences` connection, batched into one query across the eligible set (mirroring `buildNativeDependencyQuery`'s batching shape) rather than a per-candidate `gh pr list --search` loop. Unlike the native-dependency query, this check must run unconditionally — it isn't gated behind `work-links: native`, since PR-linkage exclusion prevents wasted re-dispatch rather than encoding a dependency-tracking policy choice.

Partition eligible candidates into `{eligible, excludedByOpenPR}` (same shape `partitionByOpenNativeBlockers` returns), write the excluded set to a new session-scoped file alongside `dispatch-blocked-excluded.json`, and thread it into `SKILL.md` Step 3's Blocked-exclusion report so both exclusion reasons render under one convention.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — add the batched linked-PR GraphQL query and partition step to the eligibility pipeline
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` — add a `partitionByOpenLinkedPR` function alongside `partitionByOpenBodyBlockers`/`partitionByOpenNativeBlockers`
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` — update Step 2's queue definition sentence and Step 3's Blocked-exclusion report to cover the new exclusion reason

## Gotchas

- GraphQL's `closedByPullRequestsReferences` only captures PRs using a closing keyword in their body — a PR that merely mentions the issue without one won't be caught this way; verify #257/#869's actual linkage uses a closing keyword before assuming this field covers it, and treat a non-closing-keyword mention as an open gap if so.
- The check must run independently of `work-links: native` — see Technical Approach; getting this gated wrong would silently disable the exclusion for any project not using native work-links.
- Keep the query batched across the whole eligible set in one call — a per-candidate loop repeats the same slow-fallback pattern `queue-pull-script.md` already warns about for the per-dependency open-state check.

## Original request

## Current State

`categoriseReproduction` (`bin/lib/coordination.js`) requires severity-bucket agreement (`high`/`critical` vs `medium`/`low`/`info`) between two reviewers before treating a finding as reproduced. A run's own lens-3c reproduction pair agreed on location and substance for the digest-vs-Approve finding (`step-6-auto.md:154`) but rated it high (B) vs medium (A) — straddling that bucket boundary. Because of the strict bucket-agreement rule, a substantively reproduced finding came back `unconfirmed` and needed a direct-verification override to be rescued. A pair that agrees on the defect but straddles the high/medium line is a common shape; the bucket rule turns it into a false negative that only a source-reading reviewer catches.

## Deliverables

Change `categoriseReproduction` so a location+substance agreement with a straddled severity bucket is treated as reproduced (severity contested) rather than dropped to `unconfirmed` — e.g. take the lower of the two severities as the confirmed value, or flag the finding explicitly as "reproduced, severity contested" rather than silently downgrading it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reproduction pair that agrees on location and substance but rates severity in different buckets (e.g. high vs medium) is classified as reproduced, not `unconfirmed`.
- The confirmed severity for such a pair is deterministic (e.g. the lower of the two) or the "contested" state is surfaced explicitly to whatever consumes `categoriseReproduction`'s output.
- Existing reproduction-pair test cases that both agree on severity bucket keep their current classification (`reproduced` when they agree, `unconfirmed` for genuine location/substance disagreement) — this is a narrowing of the false-negative case only, not a general loosening.
- `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

Locate `categoriseReproduction` in `bin/lib/coordination.js` and its severity-bucket comparison logic. Add a location+substance-agreement check that, when true, short-circuits the strict bucket-equality requirement and instead resolves severity via the lower-of-two rule (or an explicit "contested" flag), consumed by `skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s reproduction-pair handling.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/coordination.js` — `categoriseReproduction`
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — reproduction-pair handling

## Gotchas

- Don't loosen the rule for pairs that disagree on *location or substance* — only the specific case of agreement on both with a straddled severity bucket.
